requirements.text: A composite declares its slots and the order they render in, and the declared order covers exactly the declared slots. An incomplete, duplicated or unknown entry is a render error, never a guess.
requirements.guidance: Framework: the Composition Recipe grammar names the slots of a node; a renderer that has to invent an order is reporting a broken document.

requirements.text: Composition depth is bounded and a component that already appears with the same view in the current stack is refused as a cycle.
requirements.guidance: Evidence: Larena SmartManager caps depth at 6 and detects cycles; an unbounded composite renders until the page dies.

requirements.text: Every placement receives an identifier derived from the instance and its position in the composition, never from rendered data, a content hash or a random value.
requirements.guidance: The same document must produce the same ids on the server and in the browser, otherwise adoption and focus restoration cannot be verified.

requirements.text: Two instances of the same composite on one page share no DOM identifier, no storage key and no in-memory registry entry.
requirements.guidance: Evidence: sf-admin-menu derives its browser storage key from the component name, so two menus on one page overwrite each other's settings.

requirements.text: Views, presets and modifiers are declared in the component manifest and are the only way to resolve presentation; a template may not branch on an undeclared flag.
requirements.guidance: Framework: the smart component manifest declares templates and presentation; an undeclared branch cannot be reviewed, documented or projected.

requirements.text: The assets a composite declares are exactly the assets its render needs: nothing missing, nothing extra.
requirements.guidance: Framework: the Loader rule of a component lists every Smart dependency it renders, and the owner gate fails on a divergence.

requirements.text: A composite exposes an accessible name, and where it is a landmark or a widget it declares the keyboard keys it supports and keeps focus visible.
requirements.guidance: Framework: every Smart manifest declares role, accessible_name, keyboard and focus.

requirements.text: The declared hydration strategy matches real behaviour: a component that replaces the server markup on upgrade may not claim adoption.
requirements.guidance: Evidence: sf-admin-menu is rendered as adopt but discards its light DOM when it upgrades.

requirements.text: The same document, inputs and locale produce the same markup; a render never depends on the current time, a random value or the order in which unrelated components upgraded.
requirements.guidance: Framework: product builds are byte-identical across waves, and the same rule makes a composite's markup reviewable and diffable.

requirements.text: A composite changes only its own subtree and the surfaces it creates itself; anything it renders outside that subtree, such as an overlay in a portal, is removed when the instance is removed.
requirements.guidance: Framework: Smart Table and Drawer render their overlays into a portal container and dispose it with the instance.

requirements.text: One markup serves both text directions and every theme: sides are expressed logically and colours come from tokens, with no direction-specific or theme-specific duplicate of the same content.
requirements.guidance: Framework: acceptance runs every surface in LTR and RTL and in the light and dark themes on the same markup.

requirements.text: Without client scripting a composite still presents a semantic equivalent of its content, or states plainly that the capability is unavailable.
Event handlers bind to the owning host element and act on the instance that emitted the event, never on the first match in the document.
requirements.guidance: Framework: a nested modal or drawer bubbles its lifecycle events through its ancestors, so a host handler checks the emitting instance.

requirements.text: Structural props are escaped on render and a structural view document never carries markup.
A composite styles its own subtree; it adds no global selector, no page-level reset and no style that reaches a sibling composite.

uses.description: Framework layout grammar: document, node types and slots. The lock pins the accepted contract bytes.
Framework leaf contract: inputs, methods, events, accessibility, presentation, provenance and the declarative projection of one Smart component.

specification.description: Envelope schema, copied from ai-first standard-contract 1.0 at revision 8ed3d48efdb2435f1dd4142ab3339b00f5340fb1.

simai.ownership.scope_note: Frontend only: no data ownership and no host interaction. Interaction with a host backend is the sibling standard simai.dynamic-composite-component.
simai.ownership.origin: Drafted by simai/larena (larena-specs 5c458cf0) and authored for publication by the Framework owner.
simai.ownership.reissue: Re-issued as 1.0.2 after a report from Larena: 1.0.1 named the manifest schema as 2.0.0 while pinning the bytes it gained in the data view work. A pinned reference now names the version the target itself declares (x-simai-version), so one identity and version never covers two byte sets. Requirements are unchanged since 1.0.0.
